name: Shoulder flexion (lying, with a stick)
summary: On your back holding a stick, let the good arm lift both arms overhead toward the floor behind you.
setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, holding a stick with both hands, arms pointing at the ceiling. Using the good arm to help, take the stick overhead toward the floor behind your head as far as comfortable, then back.
brief: Lie on your back holding a stick in both hands, arms pointing at the ceiling. Using the good arm to help, take the stick overhead toward the floor, then back.
why: From the side the arm sweeps from pointing up to overhead, so its angle counts the reps. The back arching to add range is hard to see, so it is listed.
tempo: Over 3 s, hold 2 s, back 3 s.
progression: Less help from the good arm; add a light weight later.
contraindications: Sharp pain at the front of the shoulder near the end of range.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the back to go further
faults.tip: Keep the lower back on the floor; the range should come from the shoulder.

faults.label: Forcing with the good arm
faults.tip: The good arm guides; it should not drag the sore one past the stretch.

faults.label: Shrugging at the top
faults.tip: When the range runs out the shoulder rides up. Stop just before that point.

guide.stop: Sharp pain at the end of range.

points.t: Both hands on the stick; straight as it goes overhead.
Lower back on the floor, knees bent.
